content.value_statement: Complex metabolic analyses require correct model setup and suitable optimization methods. This skill provides practical COBRApy guidance for reproducible analysis and validation.
actual_capabilities: Guides loading and saving metabolic models in SBML, JSON, and YAML formats.
Explains FBA, parsimonious FBA, geometric FBA, and flux variability analysis.
Supports gene and reaction deletion studies, including double-deletion screens.
Shows growth-medium design, minimal-medium calculation, and nutrient limitation testing.
Covers flux sampling, production envelopes, gapfilling, and production strain analysis.
Provides model validation workflows for balance, feasibility, duplicates, dead ends, and flux loops.
limitations: Requires a working Python environment with COBRApy and a compatible optimization solver.
Does not provide metabolic models, experimental measurements, or organism-specific biological validation.
Large deletion screens, mixed-integer optimization, and flux sampling may require substantial computing time.
Generated analyses still require review by a qualified systems biology researcher.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Metabolic Model
use_cases.description: Load an SBML model, verify feasibility, inspect components, and summarize baseline growth and active fluxes.

use_cases.title: Screen Engineering Targets
use_cases.description: Compare gene knockouts, production envelopes, and flux changes to prioritize strain engineering candidates.

use_cases.title: Teach Constraint-Based Analysis
use_cases.description: Create structured examples for FBA, FVA, model constraints, gene rules, and growth media.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Load the COBRApy model [model name or file]. Report its objective, dimensions, medium, solver status, and baseline objective value.

prompt_templates.title: Run FBA and FVA
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [model] with FBA and FVA at [fraction] optimality. Compare objective value, reaction ranges, and potentially flexible pathways.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Knockout Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a knockout study for [model] under [medium]. Define thresholds, screen genes or reactions, and summarize essential and beneficial targets.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Production Strain
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate production of [target metabolite] from [carbon source]. Combine growth constraints, production envelopes, knockout screening, FVA, and model validation.

output_examples.input: Assess baseline growth and flux flexibility for the E. coli core model.
output_examples.output: The model is feasible with an optimal growth objective. FVA identifies fixed reactions, flexible reactions, and ranges requiring biological interpretation.

output_examples.input: Find candidate gene knockouts that improve acetate production while preserving growth.
output_examples.output: The analysis ranks viable knockouts by production gain and retained growth. It also records infeasible cases and recommends validation with combined deletions.

output_examples.input: Validate an imported SBML model before simulation.
output_examples.output: The report covers feasibility, mass balance, dead-end metabolites, duplicate reactions, orphan genes, and thermodynamically infeasible loops.

best_practices: Use model context managers for temporary changes so the original model remains unchanged.
Check solver status and model feasibility before interpreting objective values or fluxes.
Record model version, medium, objective, solver, bounds, and analysis parameters for reproducibility.
anti_patterns: Do not interpret one optimal flux distribution as the only biologically possible state.
Do not modify reaction bounds or media without documenting units and biological assumptions.
Do not treat computational knockout predictions as experimental validation.

faq.question: What model formats are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers SBML, JSON, and YAML model files, plus COBRApy bundled model names.

faq.question: Does this skill install COBRApy?
faq.answer: No. It assumes COBRApy, its dependencies, and a compatible solver are already available.

faq.question: Can it perform flux balance analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers standard FBA, parsimonious FBA, geometric FBA, objective changes, and solution checks.

faq.question: Can it identify essential genes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains single and double deletion studies with configurable growth thresholds and parallel processing.

faq.question: How should uncertain fluxes be assessed?
faq.answer: Use FVA and flux sampling, then compare ranges, distributions, correlations, and model assumptions.

faq.question: Are predictions experimentally validated?
faq.answer: No. Results are computational predictions that require biological review and experimental confirmation.
